issues.failure_explanation: Two false assertions in one sentence. (i) Left inverses of a tall full-rank matrix are not unique: for any W with W iota = 0, iota^+ + W is also a left inverse, so the condition iota^+ iota = I_{2k} does not uniquely define iota^+; only the canonical symplectic pseudo-inverse given earlier by A^+ = J_{2k}^T A^T J_{2n} is being used. (ii) The identity (iota^+)^T J_{2n} iota^+ = J_{2k} is dimensionally ill-formed: iota^+ is 2k x 2n, so (iota^+)^T J_{2n} iota^+ would be a product (2n x 2k)(2n x 2n)(2n x 2k), which is not even multipliable and cannot equal the 2k x 2k matrix J_{2k}. The correct identity is iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k}.

failure_location.quote: The symplectic pseudo-inverse $\iota^+$ is uniquely defined by the condition $\iota^+ \iota = I_{2k}$ and satisfies $(\iota^+)^T J_{2n} \iota^+ = J_{2k}$, ensuring that the inverse mapping preserves symplectic structure on the embedded submanifold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the sentence: iota^+ is the canonical left inverse defined by A^+ = J_{2k}^T A^T J_{2n} (eq:symplectic-inverse), satisfying iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification that the inverse composite embedding sigma^{-1} of def:inverse-composite preserves symplectic structure rests on a non-existent uniqueness and a malformed identity; the underlying construction is itself unaffected.
issues.title: False uniqueness claim and malformed symplectic identity for the pseudo-inverse
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence local correction using the paper's own formula; no construction or later claim depends on the false uniqueness, and the correct identity is standard.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.
it suffices to choose the simplest possible embedding map, the canonical inclusion map

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given, and the natural reduction fails as stated. HenonNet universality (as cited from turaev2002polynomial) approximates symplectomorphisms of R^{2n}, i.e., maps between equal-dimensional spaces. To approximate an embedding Phi: Omega subset R^{2k} -> R^{2n} by H o G o iota one must extend Phi to a global symplectomorphism Psi of R^{2n} agreeing with Phi on iota(Omega). Such an extension does not exist for an arbitrary symplectic embedding (extendibility would force Phi to be symplectically isotopic to the standard inclusion; exotic or non-isotopic embeddings obstruct it), and no hypothesis (isotopy class, Darboux tubular neighborhood, or codimension restriction) is supplied. The claim for 'arbitrary' embeddings is therefore unsupported and false in general.

issues.overall_effect: The theorem that justifies the composite architecture, and the dependent prose claims that the fixed canonical inclusion iota suffices 'without sacrificing approximation accuracy' (Section 3.2, eq:direct-henon-embed) and that the HenonNet-based embedding is a 'complete parameterization' of nonlinear symplectic embeddings (Section 5), are unsupported. The initial pulse h(a0|x - 1/2 - x0|) is supported inside [0.014, 0.986] (h vanishes for s > 2, a0 in [7,9], x0 in [-0.2,0.2]) and omega = 0.1, so the wave reaches x = 1 by t approximately 0.15 in the worst case, and in any case long before the simulated interval [0,12] and the displayed t = 24 (travel distance 0.1 x 24 = 2.4 exceeds the domain length). Afterwards the BVP solution involves reflections (odd extension), not a single right-moving pulse, and the displayed formula violates u(1,t) = 0. diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L \, \mathbf{z}

q_{t}(x, t, \omega)=p(x, t, \omega) \\
p_{t}(x, t, \omega)=\omega^2 q_{x x}(x, t, \omega)

issues.failure_explanation: With z = (q,p) and J_{2N} = [0, I; -I, 0], the first-order wave system q_t = p, p_t = omega^2 Dxx q requires grad H = (-omega^2 Dxx q, p), i.e., L = diag(-omega^2 Dxx, I_N). The printed L = diag(I_N, omega^2 Dxx) instead gives J_{2N} L z = (omega^2 Dxx p, -q), i.e., q_t = omega^2 Dxx p, p_t = -q, which is not the wave equation (it is elliptic with real growth rates, exponentially unstable). It is also inconsistent with the displayed discrete Hamiltonian, whose gradient is Delta x (-omega^2 Dxx q, p) -- the wave system only up to an overall Delta x time-scaling that the equation dz/dt = J_{2N} grad H does not account for. The same mis-assembled L is copied into ex:param-linear, additionally with the undefined symbol omega^2 where the coefficient must be kappa(omega) (omega being a 4-vector there).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L by diag(-omega^2 Dxx, I_N) (resp. diag(-kappa(omega) Dxx, I_N)) and reconcile the Delta x factor (drop the Delta x/2 prefactor of H or use the quadrature-scaled symplectic form).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the semidiscrete Hamiltonian systems underlying data generation in ex:linear-wave and ex:param-linear are internally inconsistent (H, L, and the first-order system do not correspond) and describe different, unstable dynamics rather than the wave equation on which all reported results are based.
issues.title: Semidiscrete system matrix L in the wave examples does not encode the stated Hamiltonian dynamics
issues.why_classification: The correction is uniquely forced by the stated first-order system and is a local formula fix; the intended operator is the one the scheme and the reported bounded solutions require, so every substantive claim survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For reference data generation, we employ the symplectic  St{\"o}rmer-Verlet integration scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: For Stormer-Verlet (leapfrog) applied to these semidiscrete Hamiltonian systems, stability requires Delta t <= 2/omega_max, where omega_max is the largest eigenfrequency; the displayed Dxx has lambda_max(-Dxx) approximately 4/Delta x^2. Example ex:linear-wave needs Delta t <= Delta x/omega = 0.005/0.1 = 0.05 but tabulates Delta t = 0.24 (about 5x over; per-step amplification about 9.5 in the highest mode). Example ex:param-linear with kappa up to about 0.142 needs Delta t <= 0.013 but uses 0.24 (about 18x over; about 6x even at the showcased kappa = 0.01736). Example ex:schro has linear frequencies up to about 4/Delta x^2 approximately 80 (Delta x = L/N approximately 0.223), needing Delta t <= 0.025 but using 0.2 (about 8x over). As described, the reference/training data generation is violently unstable and cannot have produced the reported bounded trajectories and near-machine-precision Hamiltonians.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use and report step sizes below the CFL limit (or state the substepping actually used), and regenerate and revalidate the reported reference data and all downstream numerical results.
issues.overall_effect: All numerical evidence in Section sec:results -- the snapshot data, the 'Exact' references, the MSE tables, and the extrapolation and Hamiltonian-conservation figures for ex:linear-wave, ex:param-linear, and ex:schro -- is unsupported by the stated discretization parameters; either the tabulated step sizes are misreported or undocumented substepping was used.
issues.title: Tabulated Störmer–Verlet step sizes violate the stability (CFL) limit of the stated semidiscretizations
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the described experimental protocol in all three examples, but the resolution is a routine, contained change of integration step plus regeneration (recomputation/retraining) of the numerical evidence; no new theory is required and no method-level or PDE-level claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's own convention q_t = delta H/delta p, p_t = -delta H/delta q (Section 2), the displayed H_cont gives q_t = -2 p_xx + 2 eps (q^2+p^2) p and p_t = 2 q_xx - 2 eps (q^2+p^2) q, whereas eq:schro-can states q_t = +p_xx + eps (q^2+p^2) p and p_t = -q_xx - eps (q^2+p^2) q. The Laplacian terms have the wrong sign and all terms carry wrong factors, and no overall rescaling of H or of the Poisson tensor fixes both terms simultaneously (the required ratio of the Laplacian to the nonlinear term has the opposite sign). A Hamiltonian consistent with eq:schro-can under this convention is H = integral of [-1/2 (q_x^2 + p_x^2) + (eps/4)(q^2+p^2)^2] dx (equivalently the standard focusing-NLS Hamiltonian with the complex structure i u_t = delta H/delta u-bar).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L\mathbf{z} + \bbJ_{2 N}\mathbf{g}(\bf z),

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed discrete Hamiltonian has its quadratic and quartic terms garbled: the 'gradient' terms (q_{i-1} q_i - q_i^2)^2 / Delta x^2 = q_i^2 (q_{i-1} - q_i)^2 / Delta x^2 are quartic (they approximate q^2 q_x^2, not q_x^2), and the nonlinear term is the quadratic (eps/4)(p_i^2 + q_i^2) instead of the quartic (eps/4)(p_i^2 + q_i^2)^2 whose gradient yields the stated nonlinearity g(z) = ((q_i^2+p_i^2) q_i, (q_i^2+p_i^2) p_i). Its gradient is therefore a mix of cubic and linear terms and equals neither Lz + g(z) nor any discretization of the stated continuous Hamiltonian, so the identity dz/dt = J_{2N} grad H = J_{2N}(Lz + g(z)) fails for this H.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace it with the consistent discretization, e.g., H(z) = -(1/(2 Delta x)) sum_i [(q_{i+1}-q_i)^2 + (p_{i+1}-p_i)^2] + (eps Delta x /4) sum_i (q_i^2+p_i^2)^2 (modulo the same Delta x symplectic-form convention as in the wave examples), whose gradient is Lz + g(z).
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Hamiltonian that enters the Hamiltonian-conservation loss L_ham and the conservation plots of ex:schro is mis-stated; taken literally, the reported Hamiltonian preservation refers to a function unrelated to the simulated dynamics.
issues.title: Displayed discrete NLS Hamiltonian is inconsistent with the stated discrete dynamics
issues.why_classification: The correct expression is uniquely forced by the L and g(z) given alongside it; it is a local formula fix, and the numerical claims (which presuppose the correct Hamiltonian) survive.
